18.0.0.en: 1 But thy saints had a very great light, whose voices they hearing, and not seeing their shape, because they also had not suffered the same things, they counted them happy. But thy saints had a great light, and those who heard their voices without seeing their forms counted them happy that they had not suffered the torment. [1]

18.0.1.en: Most of the ancient Egyptians excelled in the sciences, the arts and culture. But, sadly, they fell into idolatrous worship and the evil customs and unseemly conduct that follow it, so they became by their own will children of darkness, therefore the plague of darkness came upon them. Now, as he speaks in contrast of the divine light that the believers enjoy, he calls them saints.

18.0.2.en: What occupies the heart of the writer is not the saints’ enjoyment of the light of the sun, but of the divine light, the light of the Sun of righteousness, who offers them a crossing to the heavenly life in the midst of the tribulations of this world.

18.0.3.en: For they were sanctified and set apart for God. And they were worshipping God, for they had light in their region, moving about in complete freedom, practicing their life with joy and gladness of heart.

18.0.4.en: The wise man highlights the inner light shining in the hearts of the saints, namely the light of divine love. For as they practiced their daily life with earnestness and diligence and worshipped the Lord in the midst of the great light, their pagan neighbors sensed their movements but did not see them. Yet the saints bore no malice or hatred or desire for revenge, nor did they move to trouble them whether by word or conduct. The wicked felt the great difference between their misery and the joy of the saints who fear God, and between their own hard hearts and the longsuffering of the saints toward them. They were thanking the saints and asking their forgiveness for what had come from them.

18.0.5.en: * If the Son alone were not the true Light, and the creatures shared with Him in this characteristic also… why do the saints cry out with a loud voice, asking God: “O send out thy light and thy truth” (Ps 43:3)…? If man has no need of the Word who enlightens, for what purpose do the saints ask Him to enlighten them, if He is not able to help them?

18.0.6.en: So then, the Only-Begotten Son is different in nature from the creatures, since He is the Light who gives light to those who are without light…

18.0.7.en: If we need light from another, then we are plainly not the true light. Therefore we do not have the same nature as the Word, who by nature surpasses us without measure.

18.1.0.en: * The light is not responsible for the sickness of the unenlightened, for as the light of the sun shines on all, and the blind man does not benefit from it without our blaming the sun, but we blame the sickness that afflicted the eyes, so the Word enlightened, but the sick creation did not receive the light. So it is with the true Light, the Only-Begotten Son, who enlightens all, but “the god of this world,” as Paul says, “hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them” [4].

18.1.1.en: St. Cyril the Great * Since we know that Christ is the true Light (Jn 1:9), in whom there is no vanity (1 Tim 6:16), we learn this: that it is necessary for our life also to be enlightened by the rays of the true Light. But the virtues are the rays of the Sun of righteousness (Mal 4:2) sent forth to enlighten us, through which we cast off the works of darkness (Rom 13:12) so that we may walk honestly as in the day (Rom 13:13), and reject the hidden things of shame. When we do everything in the light we become the very light which shines upon others (Mt 5:15-16), and it is a distinctive kind of light. And if we know Christ as “sanctification” (1 Cor 1:30), in whom every work is firm and pure, let us prove by our life that we ourselves are true partakers of His name, in harmony in deed and word with the power of His sanctification.

18.1.2.en: St. Gregory, bishop of Nyssa * If life is equivalent to “the light of men,” then no one in the darkness is alive, and no one alive is in the darkness, but everyone who is alive is also in the light, and everyone who is in the light is alive. Therefore he alone who is alive is a son of light, and a son of light is he whose works shine before men (Mt 5:16).

18.1.3.en: * Paul says that he was formerly “darkness, but now light in the Lord” (1 Cor 2:14-15). Thus darkness can be turned into light. It is not difficult for one who perceives the possibility of every man changing to what is worse or what is better.

18.1.4.en: * It is possible for him who has the light of men and shares in its rays to accomplish the works of light and to know the light of knowledge (Hos 10:12 LXX) because he is enlightened. But we must also take into consideration the state of the opposite, that is, that both the evil works and what is called knowledge that is not according to the truth, these have the foundations of darkness.

18.2.s.en: B. A unique sun that does no harm

18.2.0.en: 2 But they thanked them that they did not hurt them, they who had formerly wronged them, and begged their pardon for having been their enemies. 3 Instead of which thou gavest them a burning pillar of fire, both to be a guide of the unknown journey, and an harmless sun to entertain them honourably.

18.2.1.en: And they thanked them that they did not harm them, after having been wronged, and asked their forgiveness for their enmity toward them. [2]

18.3.0.en: Instead of the darkness thou gavest these a pillar of fire, a guide on a journey they had not known, and a sun that does not harm in their glorious wandering. [3]

18.3.1.en: A joyful look of the wise man, as he sees the saints - in his expression - in the midst of the wilderness as guests of God Himself, leading them as a pillar of light that sends forth His joy into them even in the midst of the night. A divine hospitality on the wilderness road which they had not known, so that the wilderness was turned into a joyful heaven, not only under the care of angels, but of the Lord of the angels Himself!

18.3.2.en: By saying “does no harm” he means that the material sun, with its great importance, if it lasts a long time, may harm whoever is exposed to it with what is called “sunstroke.” Perhaps the Jews suffered from the sun. For on the one hand, the Egyptians pressed them with many pressures to worship the god Ra, “the sun.” And on the other hand, as soon as it rose they began the works of forced labor and suffered the injustice under which they had fallen, and remained so until sunset, so the sun was bound with humiliation, violence and suffering from injustice.

18.4.s.en: C. The light of the divine Law

18.4.0.en: 4 For they were worthy to be deprived of light and imprisoned in darkness, who had kept thy sons shut up, by whom the incorruptible light of the law was to be given unto the world.

18.4.1.en: But those deserved to lose the light and to be imprisoned in darkness, because they imprisoned thy sons, by whom the incorruptible light of the Law was to be given to the world. [4]

18.4.2.en: The pagan Egyptians were imprisoned in the prison of darkness, because they imprisoned the sons of God, from whom comes the Lord Christ, the eternal, incorruptible Light, who shines on those who sit in darkness!

18.4.3.en: While the wicked imprison themselves in a prison of their own making, the wise saints enjoy a great light: “Thou gavest these a pillar of light, a guide on a journey they had not known, a sun to entertain them honourably that does no harm” (Wis 18:3).

18.4.4.en: The writer sees in the people’s going out of Egypt to the Promised Land their enjoyment on the way of receiving the Law on Mount Sinai through Moses the prophet, as a light that guides mankind to the enjoyment of the incarnate Word of God, the Sun of righteousness.

18.4.5.en: * Scripture enlightens the eyes of the soul, so read it, O wise man, and be filled with love of it. For from the reading of the Holy Scriptures the sun rises upon the minds that feed upon them with discernment.

18.4.6.en: God has placed the Holy Scriptures in the world as a lamp of light that illumines its darkness. He who loves himself is enlightened by reading and walks by its guidance.

18.4.7.en: Approach the Scripture with love, contemplate its beauty. You will not benefit without love, for love is the entrance to understanding.

18.4.8.en: Scripture demands your love; if you do not love it, do not read it. It speaks to you, and if you grow weary in reading it, it deprives you of its hints.

18.4.9.en: You must love it, open it, read it and contemplate its beauty, otherwise do not read it, for if you do not love it you will not benefit from it.

18.4.10.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh * Whether man is saved or perishes, the Gospel remains in its power. Light, even if it blinds someone, is light. And honey, though bitter to the sick, is still sweet. So the Gospel has a sweet fragrance for all, even if those who did not believe in it perish.

18.4.11.en: * If a man is lost he blames only himself. The sweet perfume is said to suffocate swine. The light blinds the weak. It is in the nature of good things not only to set right him who clings to them, but also to shatter him who resists them; so their power works.

18.5.s.en: A. He who kills is killed

18.5.0.en: 5 And when they had determined to slay the babes of thy saints, and one child was cast out, and saved, in reproof thou tookest away the multitude of their children, and destroyedst them altogether in a mighty water.

18.5.1.en: * Likewise the Egyptians became unable to distinguish between night and day, and came to live in an unchanging darkness (Ex 10:21-23). But nothing unusual happened to the Hebrews. So it was with all the other things: the hail, the fire, the boils (blisters), the flies of the cattle, the gnats and the cloud of locusts, each of which had its natural effect upon the Egyptians. And the Hebrews learned of the disasters that befell their neighbors by hearing, since nothing similar had happened to them. Then the distinction between the Egyptians and the Hebrews became sharper in the plague of the death of the firstborn (Ex 11-46; 12:29-31). The Egyptians were struck with shock, and began to lament the loss of their dearest children, while the Hebrews continued to live in complete calm and safety, and their salvation was assured by the shedding of blood (Heb 11:28). And at every house entrance the two doorposts and the lintel connecting them were marked with blood.

18.5.2.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa After the nine plagues that came upon Pharaoh and his people, and that did not come upon the people of God, but sustained them in their severe distress, the decisive night came. In this night the balances were completely changed. It was in Pharaoh’s plan to exterminate the people of God, and he thought that none could escape from his hands. He had issued his order to kill all their male children, so that they might become a company of women without men; the women would work as maidservants for the Egyptians, and in the long run there would be no Hebrew offspring, so that the company would have no existence at all.

18.5.3.en: In this night what happened suddenly and in moments was that all the Egyptians lost their firstborn! They were subjected to a plague that was not in their reckoning or in the reckoning of anyone at all, which turned the land of Egypt into a general lamentation, with none to comfort and none to help!

18.6.0.en: 5 And when they had determined to slay the babes of thy saints, and one child was cast out, and saved, in reproof thou tookest away the multitude of their children, and destroyedst them altogether in a mighty water. 6 Of that night were our fathers certified afore, that, assuredly knowing unto what oaths they had given credence, they might afterwards be of good cheer. 7 So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies. 8 For wherewith thou didst punish our adversaries, by the same thou didst glorify us, whom thou hadst called.

18.6.1.en: And when they resolved to kill the babes of the saints, and a single child of them was saved after having been exposed to this, thou didst take away the multitude of their children to punish them, and didst destroy them all together in the sweeping water. [5]

18.6.2.en: They killed the innocent children, and enslaved all to their service, and thought that there was no defender for those who have neither power nor army. But heaven does not leave the rod of sinners to rest upon the righteous.

18.6.3.en: They killed the innocent children, and the fruit of that was the killing of their firstborn in one night!

18.6.4.en: Although all the children were exposed to being killed, one of them was exposed to it and was cast into the river. But the means that was for destruction became the means of salvation, for Pharaoh’s daughter drew him out and brought him up in the palace, and did not know that he was the leader prepared by God to free the Hebrews from the bondage of Pharaoh. In the water in which Pharaoh’s armies were drowned this child-leader came out.

18.6.5.en: And that night was made known beforehand to our fathers, so that their souls might be cheered, knowing with certainty in what oaths they had put their trust. [6]

18.6.6.en: God had told Moses the prophet beforehand what would happen, so what happened was not the offspring of chance, as some sometimes think. The element of surprise for the wicked increased the severity of the distress, and the saints’ perceiving beforehand what would happen gave them greater confidence in the work of God, and turned their life into a life of rejoicing, thanksgiving to God and praise.

18.6.7.en: Their souls were cheered, for they perceived the certainty of God’s faithfulness in His calling of His believers.

18.7.0.en: So thy people expected the salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies. [7]

18.7.1.en: The people did not sleep that night, for they were awaiting in faith and confidence that what God had declared would surely be fulfilled: salvation for the righteous, and destruction for the wicked!

18.8.0.en: For by that by which thou didst punish our enemies, it became for us the occasion of our glory by thy calling us. [8]

18.8.1.en: The people rejoiced and praised, not out of a desire for revenge upon those who opposed them, but because of their pride in the fulfillment of God’s true promises that He is a refuge for His believers and a support to them.

18.8.2.en: The wicked bring the plagues upon themselves, and what is destruction for them becomes salvation for the righteous.

18.9.0.en: 9 For the righteous children of good men did sacrifice secretly, and with one consent made a holy law, that the saints should be alike partakers of the same good and evil, the fathers now singing out the songs of praise. For the holy children of the righteous were sacrificing secretly, and agreed together to establish this divine law, that the saints should share alike in blessings and in dangers, and from that time they were chanting the songs of the fathers. [9]

18.9.1.en: By the righteous saints he means Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and others of the fathers, for the people had received from their fathers the offering of sacrifices to the Lord. And when they were forbidden, they offered them secretly. For they perceived the importance of this law concerning the offering of animal sacrifices, so they insisted with one accord that they would not stop offering them.

18.9.2.en: Here he presents to us some features of this enslaved people, fallen under forced labor:

18.9.3.en: First: they insisted on living and worshipping as they had received from their fathers, so that they might enjoy the love of God and the fulfillment of His promises to their fathers.

18.9.4.en: Second: in the midst of humiliation they bore one spirit, so they agreed together to offer worship with one mind, having received its rites from previous generations.

18.9.5.en: Third: that they would practice a common life in enjoying blessings together and bearing distresses.

18.9.6.en: Fourth: this society, alienated and fallen under slavery, was marked by a spirit of hope and rejoicing, for they were in fact, before the appearance of Moses to take up the leadership, chanting the praises or songs of the fathers.

18.9.7.en: Moses the prophet did not tell us of this splendid picture in the Book of Exodus, because what concerned him was the revelation of the righteousness of God working for salvation, and His surpassing divine providence. The writer highlighted that they were in fact, before the salvation took place in that night, chanting the songs of salvation, in the spirit of the community, in living hope.

18.10.0.en: 10 But on the other side there resounded an ill-according cry of the enemies, and a lamentable noise was carried abroad of children that were bewailed. 11 The master and the servant were punished after one manner; and like as the king, so suffered the common person.

18.10.1.en: And the discordant clamor of the enemies answered, and the voice of those weeping for their children with wailing spread in every direction. [10]

18.10.2.en: The disaster came upon all the Egyptians; it was a collective discipline, no house was without a firstborn of theirs who died, especially since society at that time was distinguished by the large family system. So in one house more than one firstborn would die, since married brothers were accustomed to live together in a large house!

18.10.3.en: With the unity of dwelling and the unity of trial, there was no communal sharing of consolation, for there was no person whose family was not struck by this distress.

18.10.4.en: While the righteous in the midst of their distress were chanting together in one spirit in harmony among themselves, as in harmony with their fathers, behold the unbelievers were uttering dreadful discordant voices and bitter cries because of the killing of their firstborn. The lands of Egypt were filled with the sound of wailing because of the death of their sons. And although the disaster that befell them was shared, the voices were a noise without harmony.

18.10.5.en: The Church, even in the midst of her sufferings, enjoys unity in the Spirit by the work of the Holy Spirit, but the wicked, even if they agree to resist the Church, utter conflicting voices in which there is no harmony.

18.11.0.en: And the same punishment struck the slave and the master, and the son of the people and the king suffered the same torment. [11]

18.11.1.en: Pharaoh distinguished himself from the men of his palace, and the men of his palace from the Egyptian people. And the exploitation of the Hebrews as slaves came for the benefit of the rich classes. But since all bore feelings of hatred and gloating, and perhaps the people shared in enslaving and exploiting the Hebrews, behold the trial that came for their discipline was one. God wished man to perceive that all mankind is equal in the eyes of God. For with God there is no partiality to one who has authority or to a master or to a rich man.

18.12.0.en: 12 They all together had innumerable dead with one kind of death, neither were the living sufficient to bury them: for in one moment the noblest offspring of them was destroyed.

18.12.1.en: They all died one death, so they had corpses without number, so that the living were not sufficient even to bury them, for in a moment the dearest of their offspring was destroyed. [12]

18.12.2.en: The royal orders were issued to the two midwives to kill secretly the children of the Hebrews at their birth, and the divine order was issued to discipline the wicked by the killing of the firstborn in one night with one stroke.

18.12.3.en: From the multitude of the dead there was not found a sufficient number of young men to carry the dead and bury them, so the hearts of the people were broken as the corpses lay before them, with inability to bury them.

18.12.4.en: * Then the angel arrives to strike Egypt, which had not been initiated into the mystery, nor partaken of the Passover, nor been sealed with blood, nor been under the protection of the Spirit, the unbelieving enemy; he struck her in one night and deprived her of her children. For the angel attacked Egypt, after he had passed among Israel and saw it sealed with the blood of the lamb, and he subdued stiff-necked Pharaoh with mourning, and wrapped him, not with a dark garment or a torn cloak, but with the whole of Egypt, completely torn and weeping for her firstborn.

18.12.5.en: All Egypt was drowned in sorrow and the plagues, shedding tears and beating her breast, and she came to Pharaoh in mourning, not only in her clothing but also in her soul; torn, not only in her outer garments but also within.

18.12.6.en: And you could see a new sight: here those who beat their breasts, and there those who uttered cries of pain, and in the midst Pharaoh in mourning, sitting on sackcloth and ashes, wrapped in a darkness that held him like a mourning garment, and girded with the whole of Egypt as with a mantle of mourning.

18.12.7.en: Egypt was around Pharaoh like a mantle of lamentation…

18.12.8.en: If you give heed, amazement will seize you at the matter of an incredible calamity. Here is what surrounded the Egyptians: a long night, and a darkness that light could not penetrate, and a death that felt its way, and an angel that destroys, and hell devouring their firstborn.

18.12.9.en: But what is more strange and more dreadful, you must learn. In the darkness that held them, the insatiable death was hiding, and that darkness the wretched Egyptians were groping…

18.12.10.en: But the death lying in wait seizes the firstborn of the Egyptians at the command of the angel.

18.12.11.en: What a strange mystery that cannot be explained! For the slaying of the lamb was in fact the salvation of Israel, so the death of the lamb became the life of the people, for the blood frightened the angel.

18.13.0.en: 13 For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments; upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God. 14 For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course, 15 thine Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction, 16 and brought thine unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.

18.13.1.en: And after they had refused, because of the art of magic, to believe anything, they confessed at the destruction of the firstborn that thy people is a son of God. [13]

18.13.2.en: The Egyptians relied on the arts of magic, and with every plague Pharaoh would ask the magicians to act, and in vain they exerted effort for the deliverance of Pharaoh and his people. With this inability Pharaoh continued in his stubbornness, resisting God with his pride, until his throne was completely shaken by the plague of the firstborn (Wis 18:12).

18.14.0.en: And while a quiet silence enveloped all things, and the night was in the midst of its swift course. [14]

18.14.1.en: The writer compares the state of the Egyptians in the first half of the night and the second half. For half of the night passed in great stillness, and with surpassing swiftness, until the sentence of discipline was issued at midnight.

18.15.0.en: Thine almighty word leaped from heaven, from the royal throne, like a fierce warrior into the midst of the doomed land, [15]

18.15.1.en: bearing thy inevitable command like a sharp sword.

18.16.0.en: And standing, it filled every place with death, and it touched heaven and trod the earth. [16]

18.16.1.en: At midnight a battle of a unique kind was declared, between men on earth who think that they are possessors of authority, and have military capabilities, and that they are able to lay plans for battle, and the Word of God the Almighty in heaven, where the divine throne is.

18.16.2.en: He portrays the Word of God, who issued the order of discipline, as the Almighty who cannot be bounded. His head is in heaven and His feet are on the earth. Who can stand before Him?

18.17.0.en: 17 Then suddenly visions of horrible dreams troubled them sore, and terrors came upon them unlooked for. 18 And one thrown here, and another there, half dead, shewed the cause of his death. 19 For the dreams that troubled them did foreshew this, lest they should perish, and not know why they were afflicted. Then suddenly visions of terrifying dreams troubled them, and unexpected fears came upon them. [17]

18.17.1.en: It is hard for a man to imagine a whole country in which almost every house holds a lamentation for the firstborn of the family. And what stirred the situation the more was that, as they found no word of consolation, nor strength to gather the corpses and bury them before they rotted and caused plagues, they did not know what would come after this plague.

18.17.2.en: As though their fears of what was coming covered even their grief for their firstborn.

18.17.3.en: The wise man sees that the plague of the firstborn by the angel was accompanied by the appearance of demons who troubled them, so they perceived the weakness of their gods (Wis 18:17-18).

18.18.0.en: And each one was struck down here and there, between living and dead, and he would declare for what cause he was dying. [18]

18.18.1.en: The country turned into a state of chaos, each one running here and there, asking what was the cause of this grave disaster.

18.19.0.en: For the dreams that troubled them foretold this, lest they should perish not knowing why they suffered this torment. [19]

18.19.1.en: It appears that God permitted them dreams in that night, that perhaps they might repent and return before this destruction took place.

18.20.0.en: 20 Yea, the taste of death touched the righteous also, and there was a destruction of the multitude in the wilderness: but the wrath endured not long. But the trial of death touched the righteous also, and the stroke fell upon a great number of them in the wilderness.

18.20.1.en: But the wrath did not last long. [20]

18.20.2.en: A group of Levites who envied the priests in the service of God in the tabernacle of the congregation, Korah and Dathan and Abiram and others, two hundred and fifty men in number, murmured against the restriction of the priesthood to Aaron and his seed. They presumed and offered incense, and the earth was cleft and swallowed them up with their families. The people did not fear God, but murmured against Moses and Aaron. Without partiality God permitted a plague to spread that destroyed fourteen thousand of them, and in tender fatherhood Moses and Aaron interceded for the people that God might lift the plague from them.

18.21.0.en: 21 For the blameless man made haste; he took to him the shield of his ministry, even prayer, and the propitiation of incense, and withstood the wrath, and so brought the calamity to an end, declaring that he was thy servant. 22 So he overcame the destroyer, not with strength of body, nor force of arms, but with a word subdued him that punished, alleging the oaths and covenants made with the fathers. 23 For when the dead were now fallen down by heaps one upon another, standing between, he stayed the wrath, and parted the way to the living. 24 For in the long robe was the whole world, and in the four rows of the stones was the glory of the fathers graven, and thy Majesty upon the diadem of his head. 25 Unto these the destroyer gave place, and was afraid of them: for it was enough that they only tasted of the wrath.

18.21.1.en: For a blameless man hastened to protect them, and went with the shield of his ministry, which is prayer and the propitiation of incense, and stood before the wrath, and put an end to the calamity, showing that he was thy servant. [21]

18.21.2.en: Because of the corruption of a group of Levites a plague spread that destroyed many, but the figure of Moses stands out as a father who gathers all the people in his arms, and carries them in his heart and intercedes for them. His figure shone like a splendid star in the eyes of the heavenly beings, indeed in the eyes of God, who seeks souls enlarged with love. As He asked his brother Aaron to offer incense to God for the people.

18.22.0.en: So he overcame the destroyer, not by the strength of the body nor by the work of arms, but by the word he subdued the punisher, reminding him of the oaths and covenants made with the fathers. [22]

18.22.1.en: As though Moses had entered into a battle with the wrath of God against His people. His weapon was love with prayer in a spirit of humility and trust in God’s promises and in what He had sworn to the fathers in His covenants with them. He conquered by this marvelous spiritual weapon!

18.23.0.en: And while the dead were piling up one upon another, he stood in the midst and turned back the wrath, and cut off its way to the living. [23]

18.23.1.en: Moses the prophet stood in the midst of the corpses and spread out his hands that by living faith and sincere love he might stay the wrath of God, and preserve the living from the plague that had come.

18.23.2.en: Perhaps he speaks here of Aaron the high priest, who shared with Moses in the petition.

18.24.0.en: For upon his long robe was the whole world, and the glorious names of the fathers were engraved on the four rows of stones, and thy majesty was upon the diadem of his head. [24]

18.24.1.en: What adorns the priesthood of Aaron is that he was wearing a garment down to the feet representing the whole world, wrapping himself with all mankind to ask in love for the whole world. For the priest is a father to all mankind, who will not cease praying for all men.

18.25.0.en: When the destroyer saw this he drew back and was afraid, and it was enough that they had merely tasted the wrath. [25]

18.25.1.en: The destroying angel drew back and was afraid when he perceived God’s good pleasure in Moses’ love for his people and Aaron’s service on their behalf.

18.26.s.en: Discipline me, and deliver me not over to death!

18.26.0.en: * My God, You are the Sun of righteousness, shine upon me, and all darkness in me will be dispelled, and pour out Your splendor upon my soul.

18.26.1.en: You discipline, but You give life and do not destroy!

18.26.2.en: * Take away from me the darkness of sin, and turn my sorrows into joys!

18.26.3.en: You permit the death of the body, but only for a time, while my soul enjoys life with You always.

18.26.4.en: I do not fear the death of the body, for by You it rises glorified, and shares with my soul its eternal splendor!

18.26.5.en: * Grant me, with Moses the prophet and Aaron, the spirit of fatherhood!

18.26.6.en: So that I may have no work greater than prayer for all mankind.

18.26.7.en: Stretch out the hands of my soul to embrace all.

18.26.8.en: I cry out saying: lift Your wrath from all mankind!
